dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Hey Michael, do you feel it? We've been here before. It's not a coincidence that we keep meeting at this coffee shop.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: That's right, Mira. I feel the same way. Maybe it's destiny. How do you say "không sao" in Russian?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: In Russian, we say "ничего страшного" (nichevo strashova). What about Vietnamese? I still don't know how to nói "không sao" naturally.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Vietnamese people usually nói "không sao" or "không có gì". It's that simple. I like the way you pronounce Russian, it sounds very special.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Thank you, but I think tiếng Vietnamese is really difficult. Every time I say "không sao", people still look at me strangely. Can you teach me how to pronounce it correctly?

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Of course. But Mira, I have this kỳ lạ feeling that someone is watching us. Perhaps we should meet somewhere else to continue this Vietnamese lesson?
